citation: Heaselgrave SR, Blacker J, Smeuninx B, McKendry J, Breen L. Dose-response of weekly resistance training volume and frequency on muscular adaptations in trained males. Int J Sports Physiol Perform. 2019;14(3):360-368.
training_status_criteria: explicit inclusion criterion: completing RT >=3x/week for >=1 year
exercise_selection: seated supine biceps curl, supine grip bent-over row, supine grip pulldown - NOTE: only the curl is a direct/primary biceps exercise; row and pulldown are indirect/secondary biceps involvement (see notes)
volume_definition: MIXED direct+indirect sets counted together as 'weekly biceps sets' - see notes for methodological concern
groups_weekly_sets: LOW=9 sets/wk, MOD=18 sets/wk, HIGH=27 sets/wk
quantitative_result_effect_size: Within-group pre-post ES: LOW=0.33 (a=small), MOD=0.66 (b=medium), HIGH=0.37 (a=small). Between-group delta ES: LOW-vs-MOD=0.54(b), LOW-vs-HIGH=0.15, MOD-vs-HIGH=0.46(a)
statistical_result: repeated-measures ANOVA + Bonferroni post hoc; NO significant BETWEEN-GROUP difference in MT despite 3-fold volume difference (p>0.05)
extraction_status: FULLY_EXTRACTED
notes: IMPORTANT VOLUME-DEFINITION CAVEAT: the study counts sets of bent-over row and lat pulldown (back/pulling exercises) toward 'biceps weekly sets,' even though the biceps is only a secondary/indirect mover in those exercises. This means the 9/18/27 set counts likely OVERSTATE true direct biceps volume compared to a study counting only direct biceps-isolation sets (e.g. Radaelli's curl-only design). This is a genuine cross-study comparability limit, not just a labeling issue. Result pattern is non-monotonic (MOD > HIGH), which does not fit a simple linear or simple plateau model - see manuscript discussion.

weekly_sets_calculated_or_reported: REPORTED (stated directly as 9/18/27 sets/week in Methods)

citation: Aube D, Wadhi T, Rauch J, Anand A, Barakat C, Pearson J, Bradshaw J, Zazzo S, Ugrinowitsch C, De Souza EO. Progressive resistance training volume: effects on muscle thickness, mass, and strength adaptations in resistance-trained individuals. J Strength Cond Res. 2022;36(3):600-607.
study_design: Parallel-group RCT (balanced by prior training volume)
training_status_criteria: explicit inclusion criteria: >=3 years RT experience with back squat and 1RM testing AND relative squat strength >=1.5x bodyweight; ACTUAL sample mean 1RM squat:BM ~2.09 (well above minimum) - among the most rigorously defined 'trained' samples in this literature
exercise_selection: back squat + leg press (both direct quadriceps exercises)
volume_definition: DIRECT sets for target muscle group; importantly BALANCED/RANDOMIZED BY EACH PARTICIPANT'S PRIOR weekly volume (terciles) - addresses a real confound other studies do not control for
hypertrophy_measure: anterior thigh muscle thickness: medial (MMT) + distal (DMT) + sum (SMT); also region-of-interest fat-free mass (ROI-FFM)
statistical_result: mixed-model ANOVA; main TIME effect significant (p<0.0001) for all hypertrophy measures; NO significant group-by-time interaction for any hypertrophy measure (i.e. no between-group difference)
extraction_status: FULLY_EXTRACTED
notes: Numerically, the LOWEST volume group (12-SET) had the HIGHEST or near-highest hypertrophy on 2 of 3 MT measures (MMT, SMT) and ROI-FFM - i.e. doubling volume (12->24 sets) did not just fail to help, it trended in the OPPOSITE direction on most measures, though none of these between-group differences reached significance. Authors explicitly frame this as evidence of a 'ceiling effect' in highly trained lifters (1RM:BM >2.0).
data_provenance: Pct change (calculated by this project from Table 2 pre/post means) and ES (Table 5, stated directly) both from full text
weekly_sets_calculated_or_reported: REPORTED (stated directly as 12/18/24 sets/week in Methods)

citation: Schoenfeld BJ, Contreras B, Krieger J, et al. Resistance training volume enhances muscle hypertrophy but not strength in trained men. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2019;51(1):94-103.
participant_n: 34 (1SET n=11, 3SET n=12, 5SET n=11; 45 enrolled, 11 dropped out)
training_status_criteria: explicit: males 18-35yr, RT >=3x/week for >=1yr, RT experience 4.4+-3.9yr (whole sample)
muscle_group: elbow flexors, elbow extensors, mid-thigh (rectus femoris), lateral thigh (vastus lateralis)
exercise_selection: 7-exercise full-body routine: flat barbell bench press, barbell military press, wide-grip lat pulldown, seated cable row, barbell back squat, machine leg press, unilateral machine leg extension
volume_definition: DIRECT sets per exercise per session x3 sessions/wk; authors explicitly convert to weekly sets per muscle group using a prior established method - upper body 6/18/30, lower body 9/27/45 for 1SET/3SET/5SET respectively (upper and lower body sets differ, unlike most other studies in this table)
hypertrophy_measure: biceps, triceps, rectus femoris, vastus lateralis muscle thickness (MT)
measurement_method: B-mode ultrasound (ECO3, Chison), 3 images averaged per site, single technician
quantitative_result_effect_size: Elbow extensor ES by condition: 0.12 (low), 0.30 (moderate), 0.55 (high) - explicitly graded/dose-response, per authors' own text
statistical_result: Biceps: significant group effect (P=0.02, BF10=3.04); sig. diff 1-vs-5 sets. Triceps: NOT significant (P=0.19, BF10<1, favors null). Rectus femoris: significant group effect (P=0.02, BF10=8.51); sig. diff 1-vs-5 sets. Vastus lateralis: significant group effect (P=0.006, BF10=63.87, strong evidence); sig. diff 1-vs-5 sets. Frequentist ANCOVA on change scores + Bayesian JZS Bayes Factor ANCOVA, Holm-Bonferroni correction.
extraction_status: FULLY_EXTRACTED_WITH_RAW_MEANS_SD
notes: Full text obtained via CUNY Academic Works (open access). This is the ONLY study in this table with raw pre/post mean+-SD for every group and outcome - meaning a real Hedges' g with a genuine confidence interval COULD be computed for this study specifically (not yet done - see synthesis.py). CONTRADICTS Heaselgrave 2019 and Aube 2022: here, higher volume (5SET) produced significantly GREATER hypertrophy than 1SET at 3 of 4 sites (all but triceps). Authors explicitly discuss Ostrowski et al. 1997 as a partially consistent precedent and address Radaelli et al. 2015 and Marshall et al. 2011 as prior trained-population dose-response work with mixed conclusions. Sample: young (23.8yr), RT experience 4.4yr on average - genuinely resistance-trained though not screened by a strength-relative-to-bodyweight criterion like Aube 2022. AUDIT UPDATE: the ES-formula mismatch that previously blocked comparison with Radaelli/Heaselgrave/Aube has now been mathematically investigated (see effect_size_method field) rather than left as a bare observation. This does NOT change the decision to exclude this study from figures/volume_response.png - even with the formula now understood, this study's ES is standardized against a POOLED cross-group baseline SD (a group of 3 different training conditions), whereas Heaselgrave/Aube/Radaelli's reported ES are each group's own within-group pre-post d - a structurally different, non-interchangeable standardization even now that the formula is known. See evidence_category B.
reported_effect_size: Elbow extensor (triceps) ES: 0.12 (1SET) / 0.30 (3SET) / 0.55 (5SET) - explicitly stated by authors as evidence of a dose-response even without a significant omnibus test for this site. No author-reported ES located for biceps, rectus femoris, or vastus lateralis.
independently_calculated_effect_size: Using delta-mean / SIMPLE AVERAGE of the 3 groups' PRE-TRAINING SD (triceps): 1SET 0.6/4.733=0.127; 3SET 1.4/4.733=0.296; 5SET 2.6/4.733=0.549. These match the reported ES (0.12/0.30/0.55) to within 0.001-0.007 - i.e. essentially exactly, given rounding. For comparison, using delta-mean / delta-SD (change-score SD) instead gives 0.30/0.45/1.13 for the same 3 groups - which does NOT match the reported values at all (off by 0.15-0.58).
effect_size_method: STRONGLY INFERRED (not officially confirmed by the authors): ES = (post-pre mean change) / (simple average of the three groups' own PRE-TRAINING standard deviations), not each group's own change-score SD, and not a sample-size-weighted pooled SD (which gives a slightly worse fit: 0.122/0.285/0.530 vs reported 0.12/0.30/0.55). This numerical match was independently verified in this audit round (see analysis/verify_schoenfeld_es.py) and is precise enough (3 of 3 values within 0.01) to be treated as a confident inference, but has NOT been confirmed against the authors' actual statistical code or a direct authors' statement, and could in principle reflect coincidental rounding rather than the true original formula. Left as 'strongly inferred,' not 'certain.'
data_provenance: Raw mean+-SD from Table 1 (full text); author ES stated in Discussion for triceps only; independently_calculated_effect_size computed by this project in verify_schoenfeld_es.py from the Table 1 raw data
